children: officially opened the Great Tides Waterpark on its private Great Stirrup Cay island in the Bahamas last weekend.

The waterpark covers nearly six acres and is organized around four zones (Tidal Tower, Cliffside Cove, Wandering River, and Splash Cay). It has 19 waterslides, family attractions, a river ride, cliff jumps, food outlets, bars, lockers, and towel service. Waterpark admission is not included in the cruise fare. Guests can buy a day pass after booking their cruise

Morgan Stanley analyst Stephen Grambling noted early reviews of the water park have been very positive, with ~85% providing 5-star reviews of the attraction. "While a shift towards more new-to-cruise customers could be a challenge from a booking perspective near term, more optimized marketing spend coupled with a greater emphasis on a target demo should theoretically be margin (and net yield) accretive over time," he highlighted.
Susquehanna analyst Christopher Stathoulopoulos believes the new waterpark, along with the order book, positions the cruise line operator to compete strongly in the key "fun & sun" markets.

title: Norwegian Cruise Lines lands strong reviews for the new water park on its private island
